hook_text: Three and a half thousand years ago, Egyptian doctors were already feeling for a pulse.
clip_script: Welkom, Free State. The school nurse asks questions, looks at a grazed knee, feels the pulse, cleans and bandages it. Egyptian physicians described the same steps on papyrus scrolls thousands of years ago. They treated eye disease, worms from Nile water and broken bones. They used stitches, splints and honey, which really does fight germs, along with spells and amulets. And they believed the heart, not the brain, did the thinking.
visual_style: Whiteboard nurse with a patient, then an Egyptian physician doing the same, a papyrus scroll, a jar of honey and a splint.
mood: Curious and caring, like a visit to a kind doctor.
pacing: Step by step through an examination, then then-and-now comparisons.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn to find your own pulse.
